I found one bug in the uncommitted change to `bash_completionsV2.go`. I only read the diff and the surrounding code. I didn't run the completion script.

**`bash_completionsV2.go:194`: empty completions are no longer filtered out** (regression)

The old code ran `comp=$(compgen -W "$comp" -- "$cur")` followed by `[[ -z $comp ]] && continue`. That dropped any line whose completion word was empty. Examples are a blank line in `$out` or a line that starts with a tab and has only a description. The new test, `[[ $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue`, lets an empty `comp` through. An empty string matches the pattern `"$cur"*` when `cur` is empty, which is the case when completing right after a space.

What goes wrong in that case:
- An empty entry is added to `COMPREPLY` at line 195.
- It inflates the count checked at line 202. With one real completion plus one blank entry, the "single completion, strip description" branch is skipped. The completions are then formatted as a list, and the user sees a blank candidate.
- When a plugin emits a trailing blank line, this can also stop a unique completion from auto-completing.

A fix is to restore the guard: `[[ -n $comp && $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue`.

**Behaviour change, not necessarily a bug.** The old `compgen -W` call word-split and shell-expanded each completion. The new prefix match treats a completion containing spaces as one literal word. That is arguably more correct. It is inconsistent with the no-description fast path at line 183 and the menu-complete branch at line 162, which still use `compgen`. Those two paths will treat completions with spaces differently from this one.
